reels.hook: A story Ibn al-Qayyim told about mercy

cards.text: A man was walking down a quiet *street.*
A door flew open. A child ran *out,*
crying, pushed out by his own *mother.*
He walked away... then *stopped.*
There was nowhere else to *go.*
He came back. But the door was *shut.*
He laid his cheek on the doorstep and *slept.*
Then his mother came out. She ran and held him *close.*
*“Who else would shelter you, but me?”*
And Allah is more merciful than any *mother.*

reels.hook: What his teacher said from a prison cell

cards.text: Damascus. His teacher was in *prison.*
Ibn Taymiyyah, locked inside the *Citadel.*
What can my enemies possibly do to *me?*
My paradise and my garden are in my *chest.*
Wherever I go, they go with *me.*
When fear gripped us, we went to *him.*
One look, a few words, and it all *lifted.*
Into openness, strength and *certainty.*

voice.note: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice Seff Echo; card times come from its word timings

reels.hook: The morning routine of Ibn Taymiyyah

cards.text: Ibn al-Qayyim watched his teacher one *morning.*
He prayed *Fajr.*
Then he sat. Remembering *Allah.*
Hour... after *hour...*
until it was nearly *midday.*
“This... is my *breakfast.*”
“Without it, my strength would *collapse.*”
What are you feeding your heart in the *morning?*

voice.note: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice Seff Echo; card times come from its word timings

cards.text: They jailed him in the Citadel of *Damascus,*
kept apart from his *teacher.*
*Alone.*
So he turned to the *Quran.*
Reciting slowly. Reflecting on every *verse.*
And Allah opened great good to *him.*
He was not freed until his teacher had *died.*
His student Ibn Rajab recorded it *all.*
What breaks a man can be the thing that *opens* him.

reels.hook: He wrote a classic while travelling

cards.text: One of his greatest books was written on the *road.*
Zad al-Ma’ad: the Prophet’s ﷺ *guidance.*
Not at home. Not *settled.*
“My heart had a branch in every *valley.*”
Yet it covers how he prayed, ate and *travelled,*
how he traded, and treated the *sick.*
Read and taught for nearly seven *centuries.*
Its title: provision for the *Hereafter.*
Stop waiting for the perfect *conditions.*

reels.hook: What Ibn Kathir saw in his friend

cards.text: Ibn Kathir knew him *well.*
Not from books — in *person.*
“I was among the closest people to *him.*”
“I know no one in our time who worshipped *more.*”
He made his prayer very *long.*
Long bowing. Long *prostration.*
His companions blamed him for *it.*
He never *stopped.*
Some things are worth being *misunderstood* for.

voice.note: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice Seff Echo; card times come from its word timings

reels.hook: He collected books like no one else

cards.text: He loved one thing almost to *excess.*
*Books.*
Works of the early scholars, and the *later* ones.
So many that others could not gather a *tenth* of them.
Then, in the year 751, he *died.*
His sons kept selling his books for a long time *after,*
besides the ones they kept for *themselves.*
A man dies. What he carried keeps *going.*

voice.note: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice Seff Echo; card times come from its word timings

reels.hook: The people of Makkah were amazed by him

cards.text: He made Hajj many *times.*
And then... he *stayed.*
He stayed on in *Makkah.*
The people of Makkah spoke about his *tawaf.*
Circling. And circling. And circling *again.*
They spoke about how hard he *worshipped.*
The people of *Makkah,*
who see worshippers every single *day.*
Even *they* found it amazing.
Ibn Rajab sat in his classes in his final *year.*

voice.note: ElevenLabs eleven_v4, voice Seff Echo; card times come from its word timings

cards.text: Ibn al-Qayyim often heard his teacher say three *things.*
“I own *nothing.*”
“Nothing comes from *me.*”
“And there is nothing in *me.*”
This is the man they called the *Shaykh of Islam.*
And when people praised him to his *face,*
he said: “By Allah, I renew my Islam every *moment.*”
“I have not yet become a Muslim *properly.*”
The closer he came, the *smaller* he felt.

reels.hook: Why was he called Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya?

cards.text: Why is he called *Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya?*
Damascus. The year *691.*
His father looked after a school called *al-Jawziyya.*
And the one who looked after a school was called its *qayyim.*
So the son became the son of the qayyim of *al-Jawziyya.*
In the year 712, he met *Ibn Taymiyyah.*
Sixteen years at his teacher’s *side.*
751. He returns to *Allah.*
And seven centuries later, we are still reading *him.*

reels.hook: The one door that opens wider the more you knock

cards.text: You have it *backwards.*
Ask people — they like you *less.*
Ask Allah — He loves you *more.*
Ibn al-Qayyim wrote it in *Madarij al-Salikin.*
Allah is displeased when you *stop* asking Him.
People are displeased when you *ask* them.
Every door here closes a little each *knock.*
The more you need, the less *welcome* you are.
His door is the *opposite.*
The more you come, the wider it *opens.*
If you stopped because you asked too *much* —
that is the one thing He does *not* want.
*Ask.*
The only door that opens more the more you *knock.*
